correctness.rationale: Token adjacency is determined by the common occupied vertex and the parent edge. The AA, BB, AB and BD class sizes are r·binom(r−1,2), n·binom(r,2), 2n·binom(r,2) and 2r·binom(n,2); the mixed cut crosses the last two only. Each certificate triangle has exactly one AA or BB edge. Index distinct unordered pairs once: the AA, BB, AB, BD loads are respectively nγ, α+(n−1)β, (r−2)γ+α and (r−1)β. Above the boundary the given weights saturate AA and BB and leave AB strictly slack. At n=r−1≥2 the specified weights saturate all present classes, and (2,1) is a single unit triangle. Thus every cut has at least |AA|+|BB| uncut edges. Equality with AB slack forces every AB edge to cross; the comparisons to each A_uv force both equality among B states at each i and the same B side across all i. Every D then must be opposite B to attain the value. For the boundary and below it, changing the base cut by moving one clique vertex changes its size by r−1−n; each crossing base edge lifts to r+n−2 crossing token edges. At equality these r one-vertex modifications and the original lift are distinct unordered cuts: if parity labels differ by a constant, the difference of base indicators has constant pairwise sums mod 2, which for at least three vertices forces all the differences equal. An independent brute-force scan using token edges generated by shared vertex confirmed all seven stated test values and their optimizer counts; replay with python3 /workspace/audit_checks.py 2.
residual_risks: Finite checks do not certify arbitrary sizes. The boundary lower bound on optimizer count is not an exact enumeration, and the below-threshold conclusion is not an alternative exact value.

evidence: For n≥r projection and parity give the same value rn(n+r−2). For n=r−1 the projection sum is (2r−1)(r−1)², higher by r−1. At this boundary N=2r−1 and m(G)=r(r−1); the refined bound is r(2r−1)(2r−3)/2, higher than the claimed value by r(2r−3)/2. The edge-weight-sensitive form preceding it also leaves a positive gap (its smaller term exceeds the target by r(r−1)/2).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general results cover the easy regime and the below-threshold obstruction but do not certify the boundary upper bound. The separate complete-graph proposition is exact for n=1, not a dominating statement for n=r−1 with r≥3.

evidence: The projection sum assigns each edge to exactly one fixed-token slice. For n≥r, equality forces every clique-pivot slice F₁(G−u) to maximize its parent split cut, which is uniquely clique versus independent in the strict base range. A_uv links the two pivot slices u and v, so all mixed states share a side, and any uncrossed BD edge would lower the optimum. The parity bound applied to a larger moved-vertex base cut already implies strict below-threshold failure.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The equality conditions in the prior method suffice for easy-regime optimizer rigidity, whether or not the prior theorem states it. At the boundary the known inequalities allow r−1 extra edges, so equality reasoning in those inequalities cannot certify the claimed value there. The saturated triangle packing supplies the additional bound, after which the parity-injection argument gives the boundary multiplicity.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the full boundary family n=r−1, including its exact value by a tight triangle packing, hence the sharp thresholds. No separate credit is assigned to the value above the boundary or strict failure below it: both follow from the general token-graph bounds of Alejandro-Soto et al. Even uniqueness for n≥r can be deduced by examining equality in their projection-sum proof. Boundary multiplicity via parity lift is an immediate consequence once the boundary upper bound is supplied. Two small boundary cases are already covered by the Johnson and single-edge-deletion results; the general boundary is not covered by those slices.
residual_risks: The single-edge record is same-day and only its value overlap was verified here. A stronger unindexed bound or complete-split optimizer study could overlap with the surviving boundary result; this is not an absolute priority claim.

value.rationale: The unresolved one-step boundary is scientifically meaningful even though the numerical projection gap is only r−1: it moves the exact validity threshold by one independent vertex for every clique size, separates the onset of the value formula from the onset of a unique optimizer within its range, and explains the transition through edge saturation versus slack in a sharp fractional certificate. This resolves an infinite natural boundary family, not a handful of small max-cut computations.
residual_risks: Does not classify all boundary cuts or give a below-threshold value, nor address more than two tokens.
